title: NoOpPasswordEncoder in production code
risk: Passwords are stored and compared in clear text. Spring documents NoOpPasswordEncoder as not secure and kept for legacy and testing only.
fix: Use an adaptive encoder. PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder() encodes with bcrypt by default and supports password upgrades.

title: Authorization rule that can never be reached
risk: authorizeHttpRequests evaluates rules in order and the first match wins. A broader rule placed before a narrower one makes the narrower rule dead, so the access you meant to grant or restrict is not applied.
fix: Order rules from the most specific to the most general and end with anyRequest().
source: Spring Security 7.0 API reference: HttpSecurity.authorizeHttpRequests, 'Invalid Matcher Order Example'

title: Method security annotations without method security enabled
risk: @PreAuthorize and related annotations look protective, but Spring Boot's security starter does not activate method-level authorization by default, so they are ignored.

title: Deprecated @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity
risk: The annotation is deprecated in favor of @EnableMethodSecurity, which enables pre/post annotations by default and uses AuthorizationManager.

title: CSRF protection disabled
risk: CSRF protection is on by default and should be disabled only when it makes sense for the application. With cookie or session based authentication, disabling it exposes state-changing requests to cross-site forgery.
fix: Keep the default. If the API is stateless and authenticates only with a token sent in a header, disabling CSRF can be reasonable: document that choice next to the call.
source: Spring Security 7.0 reference: Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF), Disable CSRF Protection

title: Token authentication without an explicit stateless session policy
risk: The project looks like it authenticates with bearer tokens, but no SecurityFilterChain sets SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS. Depending on the setup, sessions may still be created, which does not match a token-based model.
fix: If the API is meant to be stateless, set sessionManagement(session -> session.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS)).
source: Spring Security 7.0 reference: Session Management, SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS (the token detection itself is a heuristic)

title: HMAC JWT signing key shorter than the algorithm minimum
risk: RFC 7518 requires an HMAC key at least as large as the hash output (256 bits for HS256, 384 for HS384, 512 for HS512). A key built from a short string literal is weak and easy to guess or brute-force, and some libraries refuse to use it.
fix: Generate a random key of at least the required size and load it from configuration or a secret store, not from a literal in the source.
source: RFC 7518 (JSON Web Algorithms) section 3.2, HMAC with SHA-2 Functions; Spring Security 7.0 reference: OAuth 2.0 Resource Server JWT, NimbusJwtDecoder.withSecretKey
